reading.body:
H5 Minneapolis is a 17,000-square-foot facility in Saint Paul that qualifies to host security-sensitive workloads under SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS standards. The operator publishes no total megawatt capacity for this building, making its absolute power budget unknown. The facility offers N+1 redundancy in power and cooling, diesel backup with 48-hour runtime, and connections to 6 carriers.

Minnesota has 13 mapped data center facilities of which only 2 have published power capacity. This campus ranks third in the state by published megawatts, though that ranking reflects the absence of capacity disclosures from all other sites. The state's two facilities with published figures total 10 MW, but H5 Minneapolis does not contribute to that published total.

Without a disclosed power budget, this facility cannot be assessed for its weight in AI infrastructure. The 17,000-square-foot footprint places it in the category of a modest regional colocation hub rather than a hyperscale campus. Its relevance to AI scaling depends entirely on power density and utilization, neither of which is published.
